facts.fact: The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) went into effect on January 1, 2020.
facts.quote: The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) went into effect this year, on January 1st, 2020.

facts.fact: According to eMarketer (third-party), 93% of US IT decision-makers said they had been proactive with data privacy regulations like GDPR and CCPA.
facts.quote: 93% of US IT decision-makers said they had been proactive with data privacy regulations like GDPR and CCPA.

facts.fact: Under CCPA, businesses may be liable for a civil penalty of up to $2,500 for each violation or $7,500 for each intentional violation.
facts.quote: liable for a civil penalty of up to $2,500 for each violation or $7,500 for each intentional violation.

facts.fact: CCPA became enforceable as of July 1, 2020.
facts.quote: This all became enforceable as of July 1st, 2020.

facts.fact: As of the page's writing, only three states had successfully passed comprehensive data privacy legislation: California, Nevada, and Maine.
facts.quote: only 3 states have successfully passed legislation, California (AB-375 “CCPA”), Nevada (SB-220), and Maine (LD-946).

facts.fact: The IAB CCPA Compliance Framework was developed by the IAB Tech Lab to support CCPA compliance; StackAdapt says it is a signatory to this framework.
facts.quote: StackAdapt is a signatory to the IAB CCPA Compliance Framework and encourages publishers and ad tech partners to become members

facts.fact: Since January 2020, three states introduced legislation to tax digital ads: Maryland, Nebraska, and New York.
facts.quote: we have seen 3 states introduce legislation that tax digital ads: Maryland, Nebraska, and New York.

facts.fact: Maryland was the first state to successfully pass a digital ad tax, on March 18, 2020.
facts.quote: Maryland was the first state to successfully pass their digital ad tax on March 18, 2020.

facts.fact: Maryland Governor Larry Hogan vetoed the digital ad tax bill on May 7, 2020.
facts.quote: Which was seen on May 7, 2020, when Maryland Governor Larry Hogan vetoed the bill

facts.fact: The Maryland digital ad tax bill imposes rates of up to 10% on digital advertising, with businesses that have gross revenues under $100 million exempt.
facts.quote: The bill imposes rates of up to 10% on digital advertising, with businesses that have gross revenues under $100 million being exempt.

facts.fact: Nebraska's LB-989 proposal would extend the state's existing sales tax of 5.5%.
facts.quote: Nebraska’s LB-989 looks to extend its existing sales tax of 5.5%

facts.fact: New York's Digital Ad Tax Act (DATA) aims at up to 10% for businesses.
facts.quote: New York’s Digital Ad Tax Act (DATA) aims at up to 10% for businesses, similar to that of Maryland.

facts.fact: On July 23, 2020, the DC Council voted to amend its fiscal 2021 budget to eliminate the proposed advertising tax.
facts.quote: On July 23, 2020, DC Council voted on amending their fiscal 2021 budget and financial plan in order to eliminate the proposed advertising tax.

facts.fact: Maryland's special session on the vetoed digital ad tax bill will most likely resume in January 2021.
facts.quote: Maryland’s special session to discuss their vetoed digital ad tax bill will most likely resume in January 2021, due to the pandemic.

facts.fact: As of the page's writing, there had been no reported fines or lawsuits brought by the California Attorney General under CCPA.
facts.quote: There have not been any reported fines or lawsuits brought by the AG under CCPA as of yet.
